about: The priest asks God to look favorably upon the offering and accept it, as He accepted the gifts of the just Abel, the sacrifice of Abraham, and what Melchisedech offered to Him. Genesis calls Melchisedech a priest of God most high, and it is the Canon that calls him a high priest.

seg.nr: The priest spreads his hands and goes on.

seg.tr: Deign to look upon them with a gracious and serene countenance and to regard them as accepted, as You deigned to accept the gifts of Your righteous servant Abel and the sacrifice of our Patriarch Abraham:

ex.w016: With “dignátus” it forms the single predicate “Thou hast vouchsafed”.

nt.w020: The adjective may belong to púeri, Thy just servant, or to the name Abel itself. Both readings stand in the translation tradition. This edition attaches it to the name.

seg.tr: and what Your high priest Melchisedech offered to You: a holy sacrifice, a spotless Victim.

ex.w031: In Genesis 14:18 Melchisedech is called “sacérdos Dei altíssimi” — “priest of God most high”.
ex.w034: Genesis 14:18 presents Melchisedech as priest of God most high, who brought out bread and wine.
